records.text:
Hematoxylin-eosin staining demonstrated concentric proliferation of ovoid tumor cells present around small vessels over a hyalinized background stroma. The cells were hyperchromatic and variable in nuclear size, with scattered mitoses and necrosis.
- Smooth muscle actin (SMA) was diffusely positive in the tumor cells
- CD31 immunostain highlighted many endothelial-lined vascular channels
- Negative staining for: smooth muscle myosin, h-caldesmon, calponin, desmin, Kaposi sarcoma–associated herpesvirus, SOX10, human melanoma black, S-100, and STAT6

records.query: Need the Ki-67 proliferation index and mitotic rate quantification, along with assessment of tumor borders and deep invasion status, to confirm whether the SMA-positive perivascular neoplasm is a malignant glomus tumor rather than a benign counterpart; this is the core evidence to validate or exclude the malignant skin neoplasm hypothesis.

bindings.label: Tender, enlarging scalp lesion of 6 months' duration
74-year-old man with a history of multiple squamous cell carcinomas treated with Mohs micrographic surgery
Skin examination revealed a 5-mm bright pink, dome-shaped papule with overlying vessels located at the crown of the scalp; there was no purulent discharge or overlying skin changes
Histology shows SMA-positive perivascular ovoid cells in a dermal tumor
CD31 highlights endothelial channels; tumor cells are negative for desmin, calponin, h-caldesmon, STAT6, SOX10, S-100, and HMB45
Mitoses, necrosis, and atypia are present in the tumor
Ki-67 status and deep invasion assessment are missing, precluding definitive grading
Pathologist analysis states that negative melanoma and smooth-muscle markers exclude alternative diagnoses
Pathologist analysis notes that the available histologic and immunophenotypic evidence covers all key diagnostic information
Pathologist analysis states that the histologic and immunophenotypic findings strongly support malignant glomus tumor and exclude inflammatory, infectious, and benign vascular lesions
